# How to keep a sourdough starter alive

Baking basics

A starter is only flour, water and time. It also dies quietly if you ignore it, so this is what it needs every week.

## What it needs

- Flour & water, fed on a schedule
- A warm spot, about 24 °C, or the fridge for a slow week
- A clean jar – never a tight lid
- Patience: a new starter takes a week to wake up

## Signs it is unhappy

A grey liquid on top means it is hungry. A sharp smell of nail polish means it is very hungry. Pink or orange streaks mean the starter is spoiled and should be thrown away.

## How to bring it back

Pour off the liquid and keep two spoonfuls. Feed those with fresh flour and water, twice a day. Most starters are lively again in three days. For a full recipe, see our [first loaf guide](/baking/first-loaf).

## Frequently asked questions

### How often should I feed my starter?

Once a day at room temperature, or once a week in the fridge. A starter that’s fed on time smells fresh and doubles within hours.

### Can a neglected starter be saved?

Usually yes. Pour off the grey liquid, discard most of it, and feed it twice a day for three days.
